V.}}</noinclude>none durst ioyne them selues vnto them: but the people magnified them. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=14}}† And the multitude of men and vvomen that beleeued in our Lord, vvas more increased: {{verse|chapter=5|verse=15}}† so that they did bring forth the sicke into the streates, and laid them in beddes and couches, that vvhen Peter came, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ Peters shadovv.}}∷ {{sup|‖}} his shadovv at the least might ouershadovv any of them, and they all might be deliuered from their infirmities. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=16}}† And there ranne together vnto Hierusalem the multitude also of the cities adioyning, bringing sicke persons and such as vvere vexed of vncleane spirits: vvho vvere al cured.⊣ {{verse|chapter=5|verse=17}}† And the high priest rising vp, and al that vvere vvith him, vvhich is the heresie of the Sadduces, vvere replenished vvith zeale: {{verse|chapter=5|verse=18}}† laid hands vpon the Apostles, and put them in the common prison. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=19}}† But an Angel of our Lord by night opening the gates of the prison, & leading them forth, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ An Angel leadeth them out of prison.}}∷ said, {{verse|chapter=5|verse=20}}† Goe: and standing speake in the temple to the people al the vvordes of this life. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=21}}† Vvho hauing heard this, early in the morning entred into the temple, and taught. And the high priest comming, and they that vvere vvith him, called together the Councel & al the auncients of the children of Israël: and they sent to the prison that they might be brought. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=22}}† But vvhen the ministers vvere come, and opening the prison, found them not: returning they told, {{verse|chapter=5|verse=23}}† saying, The prison truely vve found shut vvith al diligence, and the keepers standing before the gates: but opening it, vve found no man vvithin. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=24}}† And as soone as the Magistrate of the temple and the cheefe priests heard these vvordes, they vvere in doubt of them, vvhat vvould befall. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=25}}† And there came a certaine man and told them, That the men, loe, vvhich you did put in prison, are in the temple standing, and teaching the people. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=26}}† Then vvent the Magistrate vvith the ministers, and brought them vvithout force, for they feared the people lest they should be stoned. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=27}}† And vvhen they had brought them, they set them in the Councel. And the high priest asked them, {{verse|chapter=5|verse=28}}† saying, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Act. 4, 18.''}}* Commaunding vve commaunded you that you should not teach in this name: and behold you haue filled Hierusalem vvith your doctrine, and you vvil bring vpon vs the bloud of this man. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=29}}† But Peter ansvvering and the Apostles, said, God must be obeied, rather then men. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=30}}† The God of our Fathers hath raised vp {{sc|Iesvs}}, vvhom you did kil, hanging him vpon a tree. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=31}}† This Prince and<noinclude>{{rh|||Sauiour}}</noinclude>
